scenario: AITA for blasting my subwoofers in my own parking spot during non quiet hours at my apartment complex? | Posting from a throwaway for whatever reason, just don't want this to blend into my other subs. So basically my car is my life. I have a tuned Subaru Impreza WRX STI that is my hobby, my transportation, my life, I'm more comfortable behind the wheel than I am in my own bed. Its not quite as fast as I want it but it looks amazing and the sound system is seriously as good as it can be. I live in a large apartment complex in Tucson, I'm guessing probably 100 units or so. Not sure. Anyways the complex is really cool because a lot of places won't let you work on your car, well I can pay an extra premium every month to get a mechanics spot under shade. It's an extra 2 bills a month but so worth it. When I work on my car I BLAST my system. It helps me think and focus. Also important to note our complex has quiet hours between and 10pm and 8am, I follow these to the letter but I do need to work on my car so some Saturday's and Sunday's I crank shit from 8:01am to 9:59pm. I am not breaking any rules at all. I moved in in January and this Sunday was apparently a major problem. I had two people ask me to turn it down. I totally did but one came back and said its not the volume, it's the bass, can I turn the bass down. I said I would try but I guess that wasn't good enough because he came down a third time. Finally I told him I paid for the spot, I wasn't breaking any rules, I'd only be out there until 10pm. He said his kids had to go to bed at 8:30 and the bass from my car was rattling his walls. I told him I'd done my best to accommodate him but I was done. He told me he'd call the police (who never showed) and talk to management. I just stopped responding to him and cranked my system to drown our his barking. I worked on my car until 9:59 when I turned my system off. I got an email from my apartment manager asking if she could come by. She's really cool and I want to help her but I feel like I'm paying extra for the mechanics spot, I'm not breaking any rules and that guy had no right to talk to me like that. She said she managed a nice place and she's gotten complaint after complaint about my car. I told her I was sorry but I was still well within my rights and not breaking rules. She asked me to please consider for her sake using headphones Or earbuds if music is that important to me. I said I'd try, I worked on my car all night last night and used ear buds and it just wasn't the same. I spent thousands of dollars and so much time to tune my system perfectly and to not use it when I want sucks. I want to help her out but am I even being an asshole in the first place?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the person in this scenario is being an asshole (AITA) for blasting their subwoofers in their own parking spot during non-quiet hours at their apartment complex. Let me break this down step by step. First, the person has a car that's really important to them—a tuned Subaru Impreza WRX STI. They've spent a lot of time and money on it, including the sound system. They live in a large apartment complex in Tucson, which allows them to pay extra for a mechanics spot under shade. They follow the quiet hours strictly, from 10pm to 8am, and only work on their car on weekends during the allowed times, from 8:01am to 9:59pm. The issue started when two people asked them to turn down the music. The first time, they complied, but the second person specifically asked to turn down the bass because it was rattling their walls. The person tried but wasn't fully satisfied, so the neighbor came back a third time. The person then explained they were within their rights, paid for the spot, and wouldn't break any rules. The neighbor threatened to call the police and talk to management. The person turned up the music again, worked until 9:59pm, and then turned it off. The apartment manager reached out, saying they've received multiple complaints. The manager asked if they could use headphones or earbuds instead. The person tried it but felt it wasn't the same experience, as they've invested a lot in their sound system. So, is the person being an asshole? Let's consider the factors. 1. **Following Rules:** The person is strictly following the quiet hours, so they're not breaking any rules. That's a strong point in their favor. 2. **Impact on Neighbors:** While they're not breaking rules, the bass from their car is affecting the neighbor's walls, especially during the neighbor's kids' bedtime. Even though it's within the allowed hours, the volume and bass could be disruptive. 3. **Response to Complaints:** The person did try to accommodate the first request by turning down the volume. However, when the neighbor came back to specifically ask about the bass, the person's response was to turn it up again after the threat. This might come off as confrontational and unwilling to compromise further. 4. **Manager's Request:** The manager, who is described as really cool, asked them to consider using headphones. The person tried but felt it wasn't the same. While understandable, this might show a lack of willingness to find a solution that accommodates both their hobby and the community's peace. 5. **Investment in the Car:** The person has spent a lot of time and money on their car and sound system. It's a significant part of their life, so it's understandable they don't want to compromise on that. However, living in a community means sometimes having to make compromises for the greater good. 6. **Neighbor's Reaction:** The neighbor was persistent, even threatening to involve authorities and management. While the person didn't break any rules, the neighbor's frustration is valid, especially if the bass is causing physical disturbances like rattling walls. 7. **Alternative Solutions:** The person tried headphones but didn't like it. Maybe there are other ways to enjoy the music without disturbing others, like using a sound dampening material or adjusting the system's settings to reduce bass output during certain times. Considering all these points, the person isn't necessarily "wrong" for enjoying their hobby, but their approach to handling the complaints could be seen as confrontational. They were within their rights, but being in a community often requires some give-and-take. The fact that they tried headphones shows they were willing to make an effort, but perhaps not enough to fully address the neighbor's concerns. So, while they're not entirely in the wrong, their handling of the situation could be seen as a bit stubborn, which might make them come off as an asshole in the eyes of the community.
